boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Hatcher's Run record (February 5-7, 1865) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Humphreys, the historian, is a frozen commander of this record and narrates his own orders; his account of the Second Corps is a self-interested participant's. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 48,352 (US 34,517; CS 13,835). Humphreys gives the Army of Northern Virginia an effective infantry force of about 50,000 (3,609 officers and 50,155 men on its December 20 return) and says part of one of Warren's divisions was new troops. Lee says prisoners reported the Second and Fifth Corps, part of the Ninth, a division of the Sixth and Gregg's three brigades against him, and writes of the paucity of his numbers.
claims.rationale: The frozen figures state no date or population; the army return is army-wide and earlier; Lee's is an order of battle from prisoners. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,700 total and the live field 2,539 (US 1,539; CS 1,000). Humphreys gives Warren's loss with the cavalry as 1,165 killed and wounded and 154 missing, the Second Corps' 138 killed and wounded and Wheaton's 17, relays Warren's view that the enemy's losses were nearly equal, and says Pegram was killed; Lee reported his loss small and the enemy's not supposed great.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Warren's, Humphreys', Meade's, Parke's and Gregg's reports (Volume XLVI Nos. 91, 29, 5, 134), Gordon's report (No. 181; read, not selected), the Union casualty return (No. 3, garbled columns) and the Confederate returns (No. 180; read, not selected) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
